steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Representative democracy: citizens elect MPs to represent them in Parliament. The UK is a parliamentary democracy where the government is drawn from and accountable to Parliament. General elections must be held at least every 5 years (Fixed-term Parliaments Act 2011, largely repealed 2022). | Key Fact: Parliament: House of Commons (650 elected MPs), House of Lords (unelected - hereditary peers, life peers, bishops), and the monarch (largely ceremonial - Royal Assent). Parliament scrutinises the government, passes laws, approves taxation, and represents the public. | Key Fact: How a law is made: Green Paper (consultation) -> White Paper (proposals) -> Bill -> First Reading -> Second Reading (debate) -> Committee Stage (detailed examination) -> Report Stage -> Third Reading -> Hous
